_comment: Checks for mseries-verify. precondition: exit 0 = applicable now. command: exit 0 = pass (read-only!). kind=manual asks you yes/no. 'after' chains behind another check.

checks.title: Reboot lands in the USB4 kernel by default
checks.note: 2026-10-12: GRUB default changed to elementary-usb4-test (backup custom.cfg.bak-before-usb4-default).

checks.title: Display crossbar loads early (no dp-xbar deferral)
checks.note: 2026-10-12: mkinitcpio ignored conf.d drop-ins for the fairydust presets; added the module to /etc/mkinitcpio.conf. Before: 14 'Failed to get dp-xbar' kernel lines per boot, display driver up at ~10.0 s.
checks.command: n=$(journalctl -k -b 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'Failed to get dp-xbar'); t=$(journalctl -k -b -o short-monotonic 2>/dev/null | grep 'Initialized apple' | head -1 | sed -E 's/^\[ *([0-9.]+)\].*/\1/'); echo "dp-xbar lines: $n (was 14); display driver up at ${t}s (was 10.0s)"; [ "$n" -le 2 ]

checks.title: zram swap comes up on its own at boot
ModemManager, snap CUPS and AppCenter's daemon stay off
checks.note: 2026-10-12: ~110 MB of services plus AppCenter's ~680 MB daemon disabled.
checks.command: [ "$(systemctl is-active ModemManager)" != active ] && [ "$(pgrep -fc '^/usr/bin/io.elementary.appcenter --silent')" = 0 ] && echo 'all three off'

checks.title: Rounded-corner Gala is the compositor you are running
checks.note: 2026-10-12: patched Gala in /usr/local/lib/mseries/gala for the user session only; the launcher falls back to stock Gala and creates ~/.cache/mseries-gala-failed if it fails within 15 s.
checks.command: g=$(pgrep -x gala | head -1); if [ -e ~/.cache/mseries-gala-failed ]; then echo 'patched Gala failed at startup and fell back to stock (see: journalctl -t mseries-gala)'; false; else readlink /proc/$g/exe | grep -q mseries/gala/bin/gala && echo 'patched Gala running'; fi

checks.title: Do the screen corners look right?
checks.hint: Look at the four screen corners: are they rounded to match the display, with no black blobs elsewhere? If not, change GALA_SCREEN_CORNER_RADIUS (10 now) in ~/.config/systemd/user/io.elementary.gala@wayland.service.d/mseries-screen-corners.conf and log out/in.

checks.title: Are the softer blue and red tones comfortable?
checks.hint: Open a few apps (they pick up the new colors when restarted). Selections/buttons now use a softer blue, errors/destructive a softer red; windows have ~13px corners. Edit ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css to adjust.
checks.note: 2026-10-12: BLUEBERRY/STRAWBERRY named colours overridden in gtk-3.0 and gtk-4.0 gtk.css; Ghostty palette muted.

checks.title: Network menu: speed row sits under the connection toggles and moves
checks.hint: Click the network icon: the down/up speeds and graph should be directly under the Airplane Mode button. Start a download to see it move.

checks.title: Dock: USB4 tunnel up, USB3 devices and wired Ethernet working
checks.note: 2026-10-12: Dell WD22TB4. Needs the new m1n1 + thunderbolt quirk (any Apple router id disables USB3 bandwidth allocation).
checks.precondition: [ -d /sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/0-1 ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(journalctl -k -b -o short-unix 2>/dev/null | grep 'new device found, vendor=0xd4' | tail -1 | cut -d. -f1) )) -gt 20 ]
checks.command: lsusb -t | grep -q r8152 && ip -br link | grep -E '^en[^ ]+ +UP' && echo 'USB3 tunnel + r8152 Ethernet up'

checks.title: Dock: no more failed DisplayPort tunnel retries
checks.note: 2026-10-12: QUIRK_NO_DP_TUNNEL for Apple routers. Before: ~316 'DPRX read timeout' lines per attempt, every ~30 s. Not yet seen live because the dock was unplugged when the module was reloaded.
checks.precondition: [ -d /sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/0-1 ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(journalctl -k -b -o short-unix 2>/dev/null | grep 'new device found, vendor=0xd4' | tail -1 | cut -d. -f1) )) -gt 120 ]
checks.command: s=$(journalctl -k -b -o short-unix 2>/dev/null | grep 'new device found, vendor=0xd4' | tail -1 | cut -d. -f1); n=$(journalctl -k -b --since "@$s" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'DPRX read timeout'); echo "DPRX read timeouts since the dock appeared: $n (was ~316 per attempt)"; [ "$n" -eq 0 ]

checks.title: Speaker protection daemon is running
checks.note: 2026-10-12: speakersafetyd 1.1.2 installed (j314 profile identical to Arch's 2.0.1). The DSP chain (asahi-audio) could not be installed: Ubuntu's PipeWire has no LV2 filter plugin.
checks.command: systemctl is-active speakersafetyd && journalctl -u speakersafetyd -b --no-pager -n 40 -o cat | grep -m1 'Sample rate'

checks.title: Speaker amp over-current faults have stopped
checks.note: 2026-10-12: tas2764 1-0039 logged 'fault: over current' at ~30-60 min intervals even with volume 0 before speakersafetyd. If this keeps failing, the faults are idle power-up glitches, not something the daemon fixes.
checks.command: n=$(journalctl -k --since '-2h' --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'fault: over current'); echo "over-current faults in the last 2 h: $n"; [ "$n" -eq 0 ]

checks.title: Speakers still work (quiet test)
checks.hint: Audio is back to the plain 'Built-in Audio Stereo' output, muted at 0. Raise the volume slowly in the sound menu and play something quiet. Speakers will sound plain/quiet (no Apple DSP profile yet).
